description:
## Goal
A posts a file; B with current effective read access to its canonical transcript placement can hydrate and download it, regardless of original author. A signed handle is identity/provenance, not a lasting permission grant. Recheck current access on every canonical redemption, including for the uploader; preserve manual grants, shared parent/thread inheritance, Direct visibility and exact Replicated placement.

## Approved design
Extend the existing Engine :conversation event with action: :canonical_message and transcript_id/message_id. Trusted event.actor only; confidential dispatch. Reuse TranscriptHistory.list/3 read gate and sanitized canonical projection through shared helpers; no :authorize_canonical_attachment event. Engine validates active literal Person and exact TranscriptMessage placement and returns the sanitized canonical message. Channels validates the returned placement and matches the stored attachment identity and full durable source against signed locator, then reuses :materialize_record and provider fetch.
Engine treats provider source as opaque; it does not compare attachment sources or fetch/hydrate during the read. Channels owns source comparison. Execution ownership is not required for someone else's canonical message. No authorization decisions cached across redemption.

## Scope: seven existing production modules
lib/zaq/engine/conversations/transcript_history.ex
lib/zaq/engine/conversations.ex
lib/zaq/engine/api.ex
lib/zaq/engine/events.ex
lib/zaq/channels/events.ex
lib/zaq/channels/api.ex
lib/zaq/channels/materializers/communication_media.ex
Reuse unchanged: ExecutionHistory per-message IDs, Permissions.can?/4, ExecutionActor.validate/1, People.get_active_literal_person/1, Record.attachment_metadata/1, Materialization signing/verification, CommunicationBridge/adapters, existing DownloadDocument tool. Expected no schema changes.

## Hydration and compatibility
Reuse each projected message's transcript_id/message_id, not top-level execution transcript for parent context. Preserve batch order/1000 limit, cursors, unavailable descriptors and transport error distinction. Add versioned canonical_attachment runtime claim to existing signed locator, separate from persisted version-1 materialization_source. No handles or claims persisted. Already-authorized scoped hydration needs no reverse Engine permission call and no provider IO. Unscoped hydration/handles retain author checks; canonical malformed/unsupported scope never downgrades. No skip_permissions workaround for shared access. Old rich metadata upgrades through fresh hydration, display-only metadata remains unavailable. Upgrade all materializer-executing roles together; deploy issuance and enforcement in one coherent PR. Existing unscoped handles retain old restrictions until rehydrated.

## Acceptance
A/B success via real Engine/DB/Channels/existing validated download Action; outsider denied; revoked effective grant denies old handle before IO; manual grant survives provider removal; inactive/missing/conflicting actors deny; correct parent and Replicated placement; tampered or wrongly bound handles deny; cross-connector collisions deny; removed message/placement/descriptor deny; exact UUID reads outside recent windows succeed; Engine failures/malformed responses never trigger provider fetch; unchanged connector/IMAP UIDVALIDITY/byte limits apply. Already delivered bytes cannot be retracted.

## Approval and tracking
User reviewed current plan and requested issue creation in this session. Explicitly disclosed test scenario: execution_history_test.exs test "unavailable attachments remain readable and hydration transport failures are truthful" currently expects another author's rich descriptor unavailable. New contract allows truthful A-authored/B-requested canonical attachment; retain malformed/legacy unavailability and transport-error assertions. Treat user's approval as approval of the reviewed plan; confirm explicit approval of that fixture/assertion change before altering it if not unambiguous. Unscoped author mismatch/nil tests remain unchanged; newly discovered behavior changes require approval.

Implementation sequence: Engine read boundary -> scoped hydration -> redemption -> integration/docs -> review/coverage/final validation. Child dependencies encode a linear DAG. One coherent PR, no implementation marked complete by planning. Durable contract is here and in children; reviewed plan snapshot is shared-channel-attachment-permissions.md in the user's plan panel.

Planning only: leave open; implementation has not started. Follow docs/WORKFLOW_AGENT.md validation lifecycle, docs/testing-approach.md, docs/action-reuse.md and relevant Engine/Channels/materialization guides. Write tests before implementation; reuse existing helpers rather than duplicate permission, projection or source-validation logic. No migration, new tool, attachment ACL, provider membership query, generic invoke, or attachment-specific Engine event.


Explicit test-behavior approval received from Julien in this session: selected "Approve test change" for changing canonical cross-author unavailability into truthful A-authored/B-requester success, preserving legacy/malformed and transport failures.

Implementation complete and uncommitted on fix/shared-channel-attachments. Children .1-.4 closed with test evidence. .5 remains open for PR review/post-review coverage lifecycle. Full precommit repeat passed (48 doctests, 266 properties, 11149 tests, zero failures); initial unrelated port-collision failure passed unchanged in isolation. No pushes/commits/PRs performed. Implementation reused existing Channels.Api without modification, so six rather than seven production modules changed. Plan checklist updated only for completed coarse steps; lifecycle step remains unchecked.
